---
title: Connect MCP servers
description: "Give chat more tools with MCP servers you add, an experiment: a command that runs on this computer or a server's URL, turned on in each app's chat from Plugins."
---

> [!WARNING]
> MCP servers are an experiment. Turn them on in **Settings → Experiments**. They may change or be
> removed in a future update.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is how AI agents use tools from other services. An MCP server offers
a set of tools, such as searching documentation, drawing a chart or reading the issues in a tracker.
Add a server to Fabricator, turn it on in an app's chat, and chat can use its tools while it builds
your app.

Fabric IQ and Work IQ are MCP servers that are built into **Plugins**. See
[Research with Fabric IQ and Work IQ](/docs/build/fabric-iq-and-work-iq).

## What MCP servers are good for

Use a server when your app needs something chat can't reach on its own:

- **Look things up as it builds.** A documentation server, such as Microsoft Learn, lets chat check
  how a Microsoft service works instead of guessing.
- **Work from what you already track.** An issue tracker's or a design tool's server lets chat read
  the work you planned there and build it.
- **Make things for your app.** A chart server can draw the charts and diagrams your app shows.
- **Reach your own services.** A server you run on this computer can give chat access to a test
  database or an internal API while you build.

```prompt title="Look it up in Microsoft Learn"
Use Microsoft Learn to find how Power BI formats currency and percentages, and format the numbers on
the dashboard the same way. Tell me which articles you used.
```

## Turn on the experiment

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Open **Experiments**.
3. Turn on **MCP servers**.

![The Experiments section of Settings, with its note that experiments are off by default and may change, and the Team workspaces, Migrate Power BI reports, Work IQ and MCP servers switches, all off.](/screenshots/settings-experiments.webp)

The chat composer's **Plugins** now has an **MCP servers** section, and **Settings** has **MCP
servers** under **General**.

## Add a server

1. In the chat composer, select **Plugins**, then **Add an MCP server…**. Or open **Settings**,
   select **Manage MCP servers**, and select **Add a server**.
2. Enter a **Name** for the server.
3. Under **Starts with**, choose how Fabricator reaches it:
   - **A command**, for a server that runs on this computer. Enter its **Command** with its
     arguments, as you'd type it in a terminal, such as `npx -y <package-name>`.
   - **A URL**, for a remote server. Enter its **URL**, such as
     `https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp`. If its instructions say it uses Server-Sent Events
     (SSE), select **It uses Server-Sent Events (SSE), as some older servers do**. Fabricator selects
     it for you when the URL ends in `/sse`.
4. If the server needs a key or a token, add it under **Environment variables** for a command, or
   **Headers** for a URL. Select **Add variable** or **Add header**, then enter its name and value,
   such as a header named `Authorization` with the value `Bearer <your token>`.
5. Select **Save**.

![MCP servers with three servers, each with Check, Edit and Remove: Microsoft Learn, a URL marked Read-only, and Charts, a command, both connected with the tools they offer, and Issue tracker, marked Signs in when used. Below them are MCP servers help, Add a server and Done.](/screenshots/mcp-servers.webp)

Fabricator saves the server and checks it straight away: it starts or connects to the server, and
lists the tools it offers. See [Check a server](/docs/build/mcp-servers#check-a-server).

A URL must start with `https://`. Only a server on this computer, such as one at
`http://localhost:3845/mcp`, can use `http://`.

### Paste a server's configuration

Most servers' instructions show a configuration for Claude, Cursor, VS Code or Copilot CLI. You can
paste it instead of filling in the form:

1. In **Add an MCP server**, select **Paste a configuration…**.
2. Paste the JSON from the server's instructions, or just its command or its URL.
3. Select **Fill in**. If the configuration has more than one server, choose the one to add.
4. Check the form. Where the configuration had a placeholder for a key, such as `<YOUR_API_KEY>` or
   `${input:token}`, the value is empty: enter yours.
5. Select **Save**.

For example:

```json title="A configuration from a server's instructions"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "learn": { "url": "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp" }
  }
}
```

### Try Microsoft Learn

Microsoft Learn's MCP server searches Microsoft's documentation, such as Fabric's and Power BI's,
and doesn't need a key or a sign-in. While you have no servers, **MCP servers** offers **Add
Microsoft Learn**, which fills in the form for you to save.

## Check a server

In **MCP servers**, select **Check** on a server. Fabricator starts or connects to the server on its
own, and shows how it went:

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| A check mark, and "It connected, and offers" its tools | The server works. Its tools are listed by name. |
| **Signs in when used** | The server needs you to sign in. Fabricator opens its sign-in page in your browser the first time a message uses it. See [Sign in to a server](/docs/build/mcp-servers#sign-in-to-a-server). |
| **Didn't connect**, with why | The command failed, or the URL didn't answer. See [A server isn't available](/docs/build/mcp-servers#a-server-isnt-available). |

The first time a command starts, it can take a while to download the server, so a check waits up to
a minute.

## Turn a server on in a chat

Servers are off in each app's chat until you turn them on there.

1. In the chat composer, select **Plugins**.
2. Under **MCP servers**, turn on the server.

![The composer's Plugins & tools panel, with 2 enabled: Fabric IQ on under Plugins, marked Read-only, and under MCP servers, marked Experiment, Microsoft Learn, marked Read-only, and Issue tracker off and Charts on, each with its address or command, then the note that an MCP server can do whatever its tools do, and Manage MCP servers. The Plugins button names Fabric IQ and Charts.](/screenshots/mcp-plugins.webp)

Your next message in that app's chat can use it. The **Plugins** button shows the names of the
plugins and servers that are on, and Fabricator remembers them for that app. You can't change them
while Copilot is working on a message.

Before each message, Fabricator starts or connects to the servers that are on, so their tools are
ready. When one can't be used, the message goes without it. See
[A server isn't available](/docs/build/mcp-servers#a-server-isnt-available).

## Sign in to a server

Some remote servers ask you to sign in with your account instead of using a key. The first time a
message uses one, chat says "Sign in to `<server>` in your browser…", and your browser opens the
server's sign-in page.

1. In your browser, sign in, and allow Fabricator access if the page asks.
2. Return to Fabricator. Chat says "Signed in to `<server>`." and sends your message.

Your message waits up to three minutes for you to sign in. After that, chat continues without the
server, and later messages don't ask again until you turn the server off and on in **Plugins**.

Fabricator doesn't save the sign-in. Each app's chat signs in on its own, and signs in again when
its chat starts a new session, such as after Fabricator restarts or after you change that chat's
plugins.

## What chat does with a server's tools

Chat uses a server only when a request needs what it does. The work log shows each call, such as
**Used generate_bar_chart from Charts**.

- **A server can do whatever its tools do.** Besides reading, some tools send, create, change or
  delete things in the service they connect to. Fabricator tells chat to use a tool that changes
  something outside your app only when you ask for that, but review what chat does.
- **Only tools that read.** To keep chat from changing anything with a server, select **Edit** on it
  and select **Only tools that read**. Chat can then call only the tools the server marks as
  read-only. Some servers mark none of their tools, so chat can't use any of them. The server shows
  **Read-only** in **MCP servers** and in **Plugins**.
- **Team apps only read.** In a team app's chat, chat can call only the tools a server marks as
  read-only, so it can't push, merge or publish around your team's pipeline.
- **What goes where.** What chat sends a server, and what comes back, goes into the conversation.
  Like the rest of the chat, it goes to GitHub Copilot, or to the provider of a model you chose on
  your own API key, and it's saved with the chat history on this computer.
- **Information, not instructions.** What a server returns can include text written by other people.
  Fabricator tells chat to treat it as information, never as instructions.

## Keys, tokens and where servers run

- **Values stay private.** Fabricator keeps the values of a server's environment variables and
  headers in Windows Credential Manager, or in your Keychain on macOS. They're never in Fabricator's
  settings, and Fabricator never shows them again: **Edit** shows **Saved** beside each one. To
  replace one, select **Change**. The command, its arguments and the URL are saved in Fabricator's
  settings, so put keys in an environment variable or a header, not in the command or the URL.
- **Commands run on this computer.** A command server runs in the app's folder, with your access to
  this computer and your accounts. Add only servers you trust.
- **Servers are yours.** The servers you add are on this computer only. They aren't saved with the
  app, so they don't go to GitHub or a team workspace, and each person adds their own.
- **Not your other MCP settings.** Chat doesn't use the MCP servers in an app's `.mcp.json` or in
  your own Copilot CLI settings. Add the ones you want chat to use here.

## Change or remove a server

- To change a server, select **Edit**, change it, and select **Save**. Fabricator checks it again,
  and the next message in each chat that has it on uses the change.
- To remove a server, select **Remove**, then **Remove** again to confirm. Fabricator deletes its
  values from the credential store and turns it off in every chat.

## A server isn't available

When a server that's turned on can't be used, your message goes without it. If you then ask for
something that needs it, chat tells you why it isn't available and how to fix it. Select **Check** on
the server in **MCP servers** to see what's wrong.

- **It couldn't start.** The command failed. Check it in a terminal: the program must be installed,
  such as Node.js for `npx` or `uv` for `uvx`, and the package name must be right.
- **It's taking too long to start or connect.** Its first start can download the server. Select
  **Check** and wait for it, then send your message again.
- **It couldn't connect.** Check the URL, your connection, and any key the server needs in its
  headers.
- **The sign-in in the browser didn't finish.** Fabricator asks once, not with every message. In
  **Plugins**, turn the server off and on, send a message, and finish signing in within three
  minutes.
- **The server's values couldn't be read.** Select **Edit**, enter its values again, and select
  **Save**.
- **A tool isn't available.** The server is set to **Only tools that read**, or the app is a team
  app, and the tool can change things.

If it still fails, [Report a problem](/docs/troubleshooting/report-a-problem).
